steps.name: Catch the sunlight on the birches

lines.text: Let the birch trunks and the autumn leaves dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is at the top edge, and its right side is at the right edge; it's about 14 1/2 in wide and 8 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the sunlit leaves on the ground will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the birches' shading and bark patches, and the autumn leaves, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat. Load: Wiped nearly dry. Only the tip goes in the paint, and no water on the brush. It should feel dry and hard to apply.
It should leave feathery, broken, see-through marks that catch the canvas texture. Never a solid area.
Watch out: It went on solid. The brush was too loaded. Fix: let it dry, then dry-brush the base color back over part of it.

steps.meant: Near-white light runs down the left side of each birch, with the right sides still lavender gray. The ground leaves have no pale gold yet.

steps.name: Tap the sunlit leaves on the ground
steps.part: The sunlit leaves on the ground

lines.text: Let the sunlight on the birches and the birch trunks dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 1/2 in from the bottom edge, and its left side is at the left edge; it's about 15 1/2 in wide and 3 1/2 in tall.
The outline also reaches onto the autumn leaves and the forest floor, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Brush: #12 round. Load: A light load. No water on the brush: a wet one makes blobs.
Tap with the tip of the brush. The more you tap one spot, the more solid it gets.
It should leave dots or dappled patches that get more solid the more you tap.
Pale gold is much lighter than what it goes over: expect two or three thin coats, letting each dry.
Watch out: Blobs instead of dots. The brush is too wet or holds too much paint. Fix: wipe most of the paint off on a paper towel and tap again.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: Pale gold leaves glint across the front of the ground, the path, and around the trunk feet and the rock. The painting is finished.
